failure_modes: Acoustic burst signal is completely masked by drive motor PWM electrical noise and bearing friction.
Sensor mounting compliance dampens ultrasonic frequencies above 20 kHz.
False alarms triggered by normal belt seam or splice pass rather than a defect.
alternative_mechanisms: Vibration amplitude increase is driven strictly by roller eccentricity and motor RPM rather than belt defect.
Acoustic emissions are caused by belt slip on drive roller under varying tension, not defect micro-cracking.
consequential_assumptions: Assumption 1: Artificial surface defect generates a distinct acoustic burst distinguishable from motor bearing hum.
Assumption 2: Belt tension remains constant across speed variations.
Assumption 3: Accelerometer mounting housing provides rigid mechanical coupling up to 10 kHz.
confounding_variables: Belt operating speed (0.5 m/s vs 2.0 m/s alters passing frequency and background noise).
Ambient room acoustic noise and benchtop structural resonance.
Sensor contact pressure and couplant dry-out over time.
measurement_limitations: DAQ sampling rate must sustain 200 kS/s to prevent aliasing of 100 kHz signals.
Accelerometers mounted on external bearing blocks suffer mechanical low-pass filtering through the housing.
failure_conditions: Belt speeds below 0.3 m/s generate insufficient strain energy to trigger acoustic emissions.
Operation in dusty or contaminated environments dampens acoustic contact.
evidence_that_would_change_assessment: A controlled 2x2 comparison (Baseline vs Defect at 1.0 m/s and 2.0 m/s) where periodic bursts synchronize with belt circulation period only when the defect is installed.
practical_tests: Run benchtop conveyor at 1.0 m/s and 2.0 m/s without defect; verify baseline noise floor.
Install artificial defect clip; measure whether acoustic burst amplitude exceeds baseline by >6 dB with periodicity T = 1.2m / V.
unresolved_questions: Can the experiment isolate belt defect bursts from drive roller bearing harmonics without narrow bandpass filtering?
What minimum defect dimension generates a detectable signal above the motor noise floor?
